title: Public space use bylaw deferred pending Kingston appeal
subtitle: Council also sought county shelter data, expanded advocacy, encampment fire safety education and a public consultation on public space shelter.
overview: After a day of staff presentations and more than 30 delegations, Council deferred the draft Public Space Use By-law {{vote:m4}}. The bylaw would have set where temporary shelters could be placed on city land. It will not go to final adoption on February 27. Staff will bring back a report once the appeal of the Kingston court decision is available.

Council asked the County of Wellington for resources and monthly data on permanent, accessible shelter availability and declined offers {{vote:m5}}. It also continued advocacy to AMO and the provincial and federal governments on funding, legislative reform and health care {{vote:m7}}. Staff will work with the county, front-line workers and unhoused residents on fire prevention education for encampments {{vote:m8}}.

Council directed staff to begin a public consultation on using public space for shelter, with specific engagement of people with lived experience in encampments and the downtown community {{vote:m12}}. Staff had said the bylaw was drafted in 11 days without the usual engagement. After a closed session for legal advice, the mayor reported that no direction was given.

decisions.detail: Council deferred the recommendation to approve the Public Space Use By-law until the Kingston v. Doe appeal decision is available, with staff to report back then {{vote:m4}}.
Council asked the County of Wellington to supply resources, tools and monthly statistics on accessible permanent shelter for people on the by-name list, and on declined offers {{vote:m5}}.

Council continued advocacy with AMO and the provincial and federal governments on municipal funding, legislative reform on public space by-laws, and health care funding, as amended to add the federal government {{vote:m7}}.
Staff will work with the county, front-line workers and unhoused residents to add fire prevention education to the encampment operating procedure {{vote:m8}}.

decisions.item: Public consultation on shelter in public space
decisions.detail: Staff will begin a public consultation on use of public space for shelter, aligned with the county's health and housing symposium and engaging people with lived experience in encampments and the downtown community {{vote:m12}}.

debate: Staff said the bylaw aimed to balance competing needs, with many locations where temporary shelters would be permitted around the clock, overnight-only areas, and sensitive areas where they would be prohibited. Staff said enforcement would start with education and outreach, and fines would be a last resort.

Many delegates opposed the bylaw. They cited the lack of consultation with people in encampments, the risk of Charter litigation, restrictions on heating and tent pegs, and the harm of moving people away from downtown services. A legal clinic delegate said it would likely challenge enforcement. Delegates urged supervised encampment sites, tiny homes and other upstream measures instead.

Several downtown business owners and residents supported the bylaw. They described drug use, safety concerns and lower sales downtown, and asked for clear rules for public spaces. One delegate supported a bylaw but wanted it to name designated, serviced sites. The County of Wellington asked that county-owned lands be included.

Councillors questioned the timing: why pass the bylaw before the Kingston appeal and the county's housing symposium. Staff estimated proper engagement would take six months to a year. The CAO said the bylaw sits at the end of the process and that upstream partners need to do more.

During the later discussion, one councillor questioned engaging the public on a bylaw that may change after the Kingston ruling, so the consultation motion was reworded to cover public space for shelter more broadly.
